swirendo_fdi31.title: The prepared incisor within its bone sample

Root. Hiding bone reveals the segment seated inside the prepared specimen.
Truncated and rough specimen edge. Follow the root separately from this cut block.

penis.title: Erectile bodies and the source glans rim
notes: Paired proximal cavernosa, shown as one connected source mesh.
Curve of the spongiosum into the distal glans. The second view keeps these two source parts visible.
Irregular distal glans rim. The source review records open and nonmanifold edges here. Leave the spot unnamed.
penis.scope: Z-Anatomy internal-component study. Source surfaces overlap. Urethral lumen, meatus and internal septum are unverified.

diaphragm.title: Two domes and the atlas openings
notes: Higher right dome in this atlas. Compare the crest with the other side.
Left dome. The front view shows both at the same scale.
Model openings. A named assignment needs matched vessels, esophagus and vertebral levels.
Narrow source projections. Their attachments and tissue identity are unresolved.
diaphragm.scope: Reference anatomy distinguishes a caval opening in the tendon, an esophageal hiatus through muscle and an aortic passage between the crura. Those names are unassigned here.

pancreas.title: The pancreatic head-to-tail route
notes: The thin projection matches the isolated HRA common bile duct node. Its visible end establishes no junction or lumen.
Head within the duodenal bend.
Narrower body across the middle.
Tail beside the splenic context.
pancreas.scope: Hiding duct roles exposes the gross path. The rough atlas surface and validity of its local duct junctions still need review.

heart.title: Ventricular mass and the superior contour
notes: Rounded ventricular exterior beneath the irregular superior extensions.
The superior sweep is visible in both the display shell and the retained s1233 source mesh.
Abrupt superior contours also appear in the source. Recognize the broad shape here. Verify individual vessel openings against labeled case anatomy.
heart.scope: The source mesh is an exported case surface. The views leave wall thickness, chamber anatomy and vessel identity unverified.

nose_sinuses.title: What the nasal airspace cast represents
notes: Central nasal airspace. The solid model fills spaces that held air in the scanned specimen.
Lateral maxillary airspace. Compare the broad lateral projection with the narrow central passage.
Inferior truncation. The rough cutoff is a specimen-cast boundary.
nose_sinuses.scope: The creator reports a right maxillary retention-cyst indentation. Camera directions are source coordinates, so this plate leaves the indentation unmarked. Crowded surfaces do not establish drainage or mucosal anatomy.

adrenals.title: Pair each adrenal outline with its kidney
notes: Left adrenal. Match its crescent-like contour to the upper left kidney in the posterior context.
Right adrenal. Match its more triangular contour to the upper right kidney.
Ridges and hollows retained from the BP3D surface. This exterior supplies no tissue layers or verified fine-surface landmarks.
adrenals.scope: The pale kidneys appear only in the retained context view. Each panel is framed independently.

hypothalamus.title: The hypothalamic envelopes and inferior stalk
notes: Midline meeting of two BP3D envelopes.
Inferior stalk-like projection. Follow it toward the wireframe pituitary in the source context.
Posterior depression. General landmarks of the third ventricle do not identify this particular atlas recess.
Pituitary wireframe provides context. The source surfaces overlap at the stalk.
hypothalamus.scope: Use the plate for envelope and stalk localization. Nuclei and detailed ventricular anatomy remain unverified.

lymph-collecting-routes.title: Where the selected lymphatic route stops
notes: Upper cap beside the neck. In anatomical references the thoracic duct typically drains near the left venous angle. A vein junction is absent from the selected mesh.
Lower cap in the trunk. The cisterna chyli and its inflow are unverified in this reconstruction.
Treat sharp bends in the pale scaffold as schematic path points. Diameter and bend shape have no anatomical scale claim.
lymph-collecting-routes.scope: Follow the brighter selected path between both caps. The dark body silhouette is an editorial locator.

anatomy-workshop-r1.title: The heart between the lungs and above the liver
notes: Heart surface. Locate it in the space between the lungs.
Right lung groups. The plate retains all three lobes. The liver partly hides the lower right lobe in the front view.
Left upper and lower lobes. The rear view reveals the lower lobe more clearly.
Liver below the lung bases. The remaining irregular edges are inherited source boundaries.
anatomy-workshop-r1.scope: This selection keeps the case's relative placement. It shows no visible diaphragm and leaves contact or attachment unverified.

bronchial_tree.title: Trace the first bronchial fork

Follow one main branch away from the central Y.
Follow the other branch from the same split before moving distally.
The angular underside and collar are junction artifacts on the authored surface.
bronchial_tree.scope: Authored outer teaching surface. The overview and close-ups have different scales. Distal paths and cross-sections have no anatomical claim.

bronchial-fairing.title: Bronchial fork fairing test
notes: The fairing unevenly rounds the lower junction. The angular transition remains apparent.
The opposite collar still interrupts the highlight. Small bright bumps appear near the daughter branch.
bronchial-fairing.scope: Scale, camera and lighting match within each pair. Retain r14 for the first-fork task.
